body: RBI cut the repo rate through 2025 (from 6.50% in early 2025 to 5.25% by Dec-2025 per subsequent reports) and on 5 Jun 2026 held at 5.25% with a neutral stance, choosing FX-inflow measures over hikes after the war-driven crude spike; it cut its FY27 GDP forecast to 6.6% and raised CPI to 5.1%. The rupee went from ~Rs83/$ in early FY25 and ~Rs90 in 2025 to a record closing low of ~96.86 on 20 May 2026 (reports cite 'near Rs97'). Mechanics for an equity investor: (1) FPI outflows, a wider current-account deficit (oil) and a weaker rupee reinforce each other; in USD terms the Nifty's 2026 drawdown was materially worse than in INR; (2) rate cuts help rate-sensitive sectors (NBFCs, real estate, autos) with a 2-4 quarter lag, but rupee stress can cap further easing; (3) a falling rupee helps IT services, pharma exporters and specialty chemicals with USD revenue and hurts oil marketers, importers and companies with unhedged foreign-currency debt; (4) long-run: INR has depreciated roughly 3-4% a year vs USD over decades, so Indian equity returns must be compared with US returns after FX. Base rate: crude oil shocks (2008, 2013 taper + CAD, 2022, 2026) are the recurring trigger for Indian macro stress. Actionable: check each holding's FX exposure (USD revenue share, foreign-currency borrowings, import content) and include an oil/rupee stress case in valuations.

data.trigger: Gulf conflict from late Feb-2026, crude spike

title: RBI rates and the rupee, 2025-26: cuts to 5.25%, then an oil-shock rupee slide to ~97/$ - why FX matters for Indian equity returns
